free_tier.stated: none: OCI DNS requires a paid OCI account, either as a pay-as-you-go or Universal Credits contract

per_object_cap.stated: zone file uploads are limited to 1 megabyte (MB) in size per zone file; a zone holds up to 25,000 records
per_object_cap.notes: a zone file over 1 MB must be split; records can be added in batches of 100 through the PatchDomainRecords API

retention.stated: a zone persists until the user deletes it; no inactivity deletion rule was stated on the pages read

egress.terms: DNS queries are metered and billed per 1,000,000 queries; the price-list unit price cell is blank on the first-party page, so no marginal price is recorded

interface_detail: the browser-based Console, a REST API, the OCI CLI and OCI SDKs; access is authenticated through OCI IAM, and zones are managed through the Console, CLI or API
tooling: the OCI CLI (oci dns ...), OCI SDKs, BIND-compatible zone-file import and export, the OCI Terraform provider, and Kubernetes ExternalDNS
chaining: managed authoritative DNS for a domain registered at an external registrar, with primary and secondary zones for redundancy and traffic steering by endpoint health, geography, ASN or source prefix; it integrates with Kubernetes ExternalDNS, but unlike the free managed DNS options in this topic it is a paid OCI service

limits.value: 25,000 records per zone; zone file uploads limited to 1 megabyte (MB) per zone file
public DNS zones are only supported in the OC1 commercial realm; a domain must be registered and delegated at an external registrar, as OCI isn't a registrar

binding_note: the service is paid-only with no free tier, so no published quota binds a free user; the paid-account and card requirement is the real gate, and the 1000-zone and 25,000-record caps are far above one user's needs

identity_cost.detail: OCI DNS requires a paid OCI account on a pay-as-you-go or Universal Credits contract. The Oracle Cloud signup asks for a credit or debit card used for account setup and identity verification, and accepts credit cards and debit cards that function like credit cards, not debit cards with a PIN or virtual, single-use or prepaid cards. A domain registered and delegated at an external registrar is needed for a public zone since OCI isn't a registrar.

reliability_note: zone files over 1 MB must be split into batches of 100 records for upload; public DNS zones are only supported in the OC1 commercial realm, and Traffic Management is unavailable on private zones; no outage history was read
confidence_note: the Oracle DNS product page, the OCI price list, the DNS overview, zone-management and getting-started docs, the DNS cost estimator and the Oracle Cloud free tier/signup page were captured and quoted. No marginal per-query price is published on the first-party pages read (the price-list unit price cell is blank), so none is recorded.
